title: People's Republic of China
capsule: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed on 1 October 1949 by Mao Zedong in Beijing following the Communist Party's victory over the Nationalist government, which retreated to Taiwan. Mao's era saw radical collectivization in the Great Leap Forward (1958–1962) and the Cultural Revolution (1966–1976), each causing millions of deaths; Deng Xiaoping's post-1978 reforms shifted the country toward a socialist market economy that produced the most rapid sustained economic growth in modern history. By the early twenty-first century the PRC had become the world's second-largest economy and a major military power, asserting territorial claims in the South China Sea and pressing its position on Taiwan throughout the attested span.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Modern territorial extent is well-documented by authoritative geographic datasets; contested boundaries with India (Aksai Chin, Arunachal Pradesh), Taiwan, and South China Sea claimants mean some perimeter zones carry genuine ambiguity.
